segments.title: 第22章 應志誠回家
segments.content:
Return of the Verdant Era Chapter 22: Ying Zhicheng Comes Home

Inside the Wenyue Group in Changning City.

Hongdou, the editor-in-chief of the Urban genre division, was looking at the list of Sanjiang recommendations submitted by several editors.

Each editor submitted three books, totaling just over ten books.

This period, there were 83 new books in the Urban category still being serialized, and 124 that had been dropped.

Among the remaining 83 books, all had exceeded 150,000 words.

Among them, 65 books had fewer than 100 concurrent readers.

There were 12 books with 100 to 500 concurrent readers.

There were 5 books with 500 to 1,000 concurrent readers.

And only one book had over 1,000 concurrent readers.

Concurrent readership refers to the number of readers who have read the latest chapter of the book within 24 hours.

Generally speaking, when a novel goes on sale, the number of readers willing to pay for a subscription is roughly between sixty and eighty percent of the concurrent readership.

No major authors had released new books in the Urban category this week, so these figures were actually quite good.

Especially this new book with over 1,000 concurrent readers. It seemed the author was a newcomer?

Hongdou clicked on the book and glanced through it. By the time she came to her senses, more than half an hour had passed.

"All division EICs, let's have a meeting to finalize the Sanjiang recommendation list." Wenyue's chief editor, Nanfeng, walked to the office, knocked on the door, and said.

The EICs of each division rose and took their seats in the conference room, beginning a passionate debate, vying for the Sanjiang recommendation spots.

When Hongdou returned to the editorial team looking exhausted, she sent a notice to several editors.

The Urban division gets two Sanjiang spots next week. One goes to Scion of a Medical Family, the other to I'm Really Not a Star. The lists for the other divisions have been sent to you as well.

As soon as this notice was sent, editor Qingyue, who had been looking confident just moments before, froze, her expression one of disbelief.

"EIC, what's going on?" editor Qingyue asked with a frown. "This Hallyu Max-Level Guide in my hands has 780 concurrent readers. Those numbers would have been a shoo-in for Sanjiang in previous weeks, right? There aren't any particularly hot books this week either."

"Just bad luck. Tell the author to wait another week, or they'll have to go straight on sale," editor-in-chief Hongdou said without lifting her eyes. "Xuanhuan, Xianxia, and Sci-Fi all have several books with over 800 concurrent readers this time. Our division couldn't compete this week, so we only got two spots."

"That fierce?" Editor Qingyue was stunned. "Wait, that's not right. I know about Scion of a Medical Family, its concurrent readership was high before, so it's understandable it's number one this week. But what's the deal with that I'm Really Not a Star?"

"Judging by the title, it's also about the entertainment industry, right?"

"Is there another Hallyu novel this week that I don't know about?"

"Ahem." Qianzhou, an editor to the side, couldn't help but speak up. "Sister Yue, that one's mine. It's an alternate-universe entertainment novel, not a Hallyu one."

"Not a Hallyu novel?!" Editor Qingyue's face was filled with astonishment. "Which veteran author wrote it?"

Based on her experience over the past six months, Hallyu novels basically dominated the entertainment genre.

Unless it was a new book specifically launched by a veteran entertainment author, a new book by a newcomer would inevitably be crushed by Hallyu novels.

Without exception.

"Just a new author I fished out of the new book pool." Editor Qianzhou gave a silly, harmless smile and said, "Remember what happened at the end of last month? There was an author who hadn't signed a contract, and it turned out we all sent him a contract offer."

"Oh, I think so." Editor Qingyue looked a little hazy, having a vague impression of the matter.

"This is the book written by that author," editor Qianzhou explained. "Since the author is a minor, it took some time to convince his family, so the contract was delayed by a week."

As he said this.

Editor-in-chief Hongdou, who was still sipping her tea, suddenly spat out a mouthful of water.

"Cough, cough!" Editor-in-chief Hongdou coughed hard, her previously calm expression now full of shock. "What did you just say? A minor? A minor could write this book?"

Before the meeting, Hongdou had taken a look at the book and had gotten completely sucked in, only snapping out of it after half an hour.

The book started with a strong gimmick, kicking off with a bang at a pop queen's concert.

But in editor-in-chief Hongdou's view, what was truly impressive was the protagonist's style of doing things and his logic, both of which had a strong flavor of maturity.

Especially in the opening segment, the protagonist goes on stage as a lucky audience member at a pop queen's concert and performs a new song.

The song he chose wasn't random; its musical style corresponded perfectly with the pop queen's latest album.

He piqued the pop queen's interest, followed up with negotiations for the song's copyright, and then used the song as a breakthrough to obtain a series of resources from her.

The copyright fee was secondary; the key was the connection to the pop queen and the allocation of other industry resources.

This instantly opened up the protagonist's future path and broadened his horizons.

This was clearly the work of a seasoned entertainment writer, some veteran using a new pen name.

And now you're telling me this thing was written by a minor?!

"Yeah." Editor Qianzhou scratched his head. "This author, with the pen name Chong Ran, I checked his contract information. He's definitely a minor, 15 years old this year."

At this, no one in the editorial team spoke. They all looked at each other, not expecting to encounter such a talented freak in this day and age.

"Oh, right." Editor Qianzhou suddenly remembered something, glanced at the list of new books in his charge for this period, and added, "There's also that Arts and Literature Era. It has over five hundred concurrent readers this week, and the author is also a minor... 17 years old, and a girl at that."

"Huh?"

The editors present were all stunned, looking at Qianzhou with a somewhat strange expression.

Kid, it's understandable that you don't have author resources as a newcomer.

But you don't have to exclusively target minors, do you?!

Are you trying to nurture them from scratch or something?

...

Early August.

The weather grew increasingly hot.

Li Luo worked all morning at the breakfast shop, his back drenched in sweat, his T-shirt completely soaked.

While eating lunch in the shop, Li Luo sat at a table, watching his parents bustling about inside.

Sweat streamed down their foreheads. For over a decade, day in and day out, this was how they lived.

He had only been helping out for a little over a month during the summer break, and now he felt exhausted every time he got up.

At this thought, Li Luo pursed his lips, finally feeling a deep empathy for his parents' hardship.

If possible, he had to work harder, to try and free his parents from this repetitive and arduous work.

With these thoughts in mind, Li Luo finished his lunch, and the phone in his pocket suddenly vibrated.

The phone he was using now was a flip phone his mom had retired.

Flipping it open, he saw it was a call from Ying Chanxi. Li Luo raised an eyebrow, answered it, and put it to his ear.

"Hello? What's up?"

"Li Luo, where are you right now?" Ying Chanxi asked in a low voice on the other end of the line.

"At the shop, why? Aren't you in class?" Li Luo asked, looking puzzled.

"I am. It's lunch break now," Ying Chanxi replied. "I saw the weather forecast yesterday, and it said it's going to rain today. I forgot to bring in the clothes I hung out to dry, and the balcony window is also open. Can you go back and help me get them later?"

"Oh, got it." Li Luo nodded. "Anything else?"

"Hmm..." Ying Chanxi thought for a moment. "These two days are the all-subject tests for the advance class. Just wish me luck."

"I think with your ability, getting first place should still be a piece of cake."

"So?"

"Then I wish fellow student Ying Chanxi first place in all subjects. That's more challenging," Li Luo grinned and chuckled. "Good luck."

"Uh-huh." Ying Chanxi nodded with satisfaction. "Just you wait, I'll give it a try."

After hanging up, Li Luo stretched, glanced at the somewhat gloomy sky outside, and felt that it was probably about to rain.

"Mom, did you bring an umbrella?" Li Luo asked Lin Xiuhong before he left.

"No, why?"

"It might rain this afternoon," Li Luo said. "I'm heading back now. If it's raining in the evening, give me a call, and I'll bring an umbrella down."

"Got it, you can go."

Watching her son's back as he left the shop, Lin Xiuhong wiped the sweat from her forehead, feeling as if her exhaustion wasn't as heavy as it used to be.

At first, she thought the boy was just putting on an act, wanting to make a good impression on his parents at the beginning of the summer break to get some more pocket money.

Even so, Lin Xiuhong felt that even if it was just for show, it was a change for the better, so she was very supportive and encouraging.

She just didn't expect Li Luo to actually come to the breakfast shop to help them every single morning.

And this help had lasted for over a month.

From the looks of it, he probably didn't plan to rest until high school started.

Every time she thought of this, Lin Xiuhong's face would fill with a sense of relief.

Just then, Li Guohong came out of the kitchen, washed his hands in the sink, wiped them twice on his apron, and said as he walked over:

"Your younger uncle just called. He said the loan has come through and told me to set a time for us to go and handle the transfer of ownership."

"Oh, that was fast." Hearing this news, a smile appeared on Lin Xiuhong's face as well. "How about this weekend then?"

"That's what I was thinking too." Li Guohong nodded. "Oh right, Zhicheng sent me a message saying he's coming back today. He invited us to his place for dinner and told me not to tell Xixi yet."

"He's finally willing to come back, huh?" Lin Xiuhong frowned when she heard that Ying Zhicheng was coming back. "It's been several months again since he was last here. Is his work more important than his daughter?"

"He's at a big company, it's normal to be busy," Li Guohong said, shaking his head. "Besides, Xixi is very well-behaved and does well in her studies, so he doesn't have to worry about her."

"But he still can't just not be there for her all the time." Lin Xiuhong thought like a woman; whenever she thought about how Ying Chanxi had no parents around on a daily basis and was still so well-behaved, she felt a pang of heartache. "At least he knows to come back."

On the other side.

Li Luo had already returned to Jincheng Residential Complex. He made his way to the fourth floor, took out the key to Ying Chanxi's home from inside the door couplet, opened the door, and walked in.

The weather had completely turned gloomy, and a light drizzle was falling from the sky.

Li Luo hurried to the balcony and closed the window first.

Then he looked up and took down all the clothes Ying Chanxi had hung out to dry.

"She really doesn't know how to avoid suspicion," Li Luo shook his head with a helpless expression, gathering some cute little items along with the clothes and pants into his arms. He planned to put them on Ying Chanxi's bed for her to sort out when she got back.

He couldn't help but mutter, "Why does she like Pikachu so much?"

But just as he walked from the balcony into the living room, about to head into Ying Chanxi's bedroom, he suddenly heard the sound of a key in the lock at the front door.

This made Li Luo freeze.

Didn't she say she had tests?

Why is she back at noon?

As Li Luo was thinking this, the door had already been opened.

The figure of a middle-aged man walked in from outside.

Ying Zhicheng was dressed in a crisp suit, with a neatly trimmed beard and short, layered hair, giving him a very distinguished look.

After entering, he habitually took off his shoes. Looking down, he couldn't find the pair of blue slippers he usually wore.

But in the next second, he found them.

Ying Zhicheng looked at the boy wearing those blue slippers, and at the pile of girl's clothes he was holding in his arms, and for a moment, he was lost in thought.

"Yo, Uncle Ying." Li Luo greeted him a bit awkwardly. "You're back?"
